Source: wash2/accesskit cosmic-0.14, commit f0599eed5f18111228266fe3f28991cc48b5964f.

Local patch adds AT-SPI EditableText to writable text controls explicitly supporting string SetValue. The supported method is SetTextContents, dispatched as Action::SetValue with string data. InsertText, DeleteText, clipboard and attribute editing explicitly return false; this patch does not claim those operations are implemented. The existing Text interface continues to provide caret and selection operations when the control advertises SetTextSelection.

Local patch also keeps the adapter context alive when the D-Bus session bus, the AT-SPI bus launcher or the AT-SPI bus is unreachable (cagents #1170). The pinned upstream unwraps the event loop's result, so a refused AT-SPI connection panics the context thread and disables accessibility for the rest of the process ([accesskit#727](https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit/issues/727)), and a missing session bus ends the thread without retrying. Upstream [accesskit#741](https://github.com/AccessKit/accesskit/pull/741), merged after the pinned tag, stops the panic but does not reconnect: a failed AT-SPI connection leaves adapters inactive until the screen-reader status changes, and an event-loop error ends the context. This patch instead:

- Keeps adapters and the message receiver across outages. Adapters are deactivated while no AT-SPI bus is connected and asked for a fresh initial tree once one is. On disconnection, queued messages are processed as though no bus were connected, which keeps adapter additions and removals and drops updates for the lost bus; activation registers each tree afresh, and a stale update applied first would leave its node defunct on the next bus.
- Detects lost connections through zbus `Connection::closed` and `Connection::is_closed`, which need zbus 5.18 or later, and through I/O errors from adapter messages. Other failures of a single request are debug messages and leave the connection up.
- Bounds each method call (`method_timeout`), each connection attempt and each adapter message by 10 seconds, so an unresponsive bus, launcher or registry is treated as unreachable rather than holding up the context.
- Retries after 1 second, doubling to at most 30 seconds. The session and AT-SPI buses back off independently, and an unanswered screen-reader status from a running launcher is retried with the AT-SPI bus. The first failure of an outage is a `tracing` warning and later attempts are debug messages. An outage ends only once a connection stays up for 30 seconds; launcher restarts, screen-reader toggles, session-bus loss and connections that drop at once keep its backoff and warning. A pending AT-SPI retry keeps its time while the screen reader is disabled or the session bus is lost, and is waited for only while there is something to retry, so no launcher or screen-reader change brings it forward.
- Watches the owner of `org.a11y.Bus`, so a launcher that starts late, leaves or restarts is followed without polling. An unreadable screen-reader status deactivates adapters and retries the status read, including when a property invalidation cannot be refreshed and the launcher sends no further changes. Retries stop while the screen reader is explicitly disabled, and the context returns once every message sender is dropped.

The `async-io` feature waits with `async_io::Timer`; `futures-util` and `tokio-stream` are no longer used. Remove this part when upstream reconnects equivalently; accesskit#741 alone does not.

The tests for this part re-execute the test binary per scenario with private `dbus-daemon` buses, so they never contact the user's buses. Without `dbus-daemon` they are skipped. Each daemon and isolated process is killed with the test that started it, and each temporary directory stays locked while in use, so a later run removes only the directories of runs that were killed. Run them with `tokio`, as the application ships, from the workspace root with `cargo test --locked -p accesskit_unix`. Cargo cannot select features for this package from the workspace, so to run them with `async-io`, copy `vendor/accesskit-unix` and `vendor/accesskit-atspi-common` into an empty directory, append an empty `[workspace]` table to the copied `accesskit-unix/Cargo.toml`, copy `Cargo.lock` beside it and run `cargo test --offline` there. The Linux UI diagnostics regression selects the same adapter through the existing Git-source patch; the CLI and host features do not select it.

The two crate manifests are standalone copies of the pinned workspace manifests; the common/consumer types stay at the exact same Git tag and lock revision. The accesskit-unix manifest adds `tracing` and, for `async-io`, `async-io`, both already in the dependency graph; drops `futures-util` and `tokio-stream`; and requires zbus 5.18. Upstream license files are retained. Remove the EditableText part when the pinned Linux adapter provides equivalent string replacement. No ABI or wire protocol change is introduced.
